newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-SINGH BORROWS CLUB TO WIN SOUTH AFRICAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SINGH BORROWS CLUB TO WIN SOUTH AFRICAN OPEN.

text.p: Fiji's Vijay Singh posted a 69 for a thrilling single-shot victory over Nick Price of Zimbabwe in the final round of the 3.4 million rand ($745,000) South African Open on Sunday.
Singh, who had an 18-under-par aggregate of 270, was quick to attribute his success to a borrowed driver and a short putter.

The tournament started inauspiciously for the Fijian, who cracked his driver on the practice range on Thursday. But minutes before he was due to tee off, American fellow professional Bruce Vaughan lent him his spare.
"Bruce gave me his spare driver even though I was unfamiliar with it but it went straight throughout the week," Singh said after collecting the trophy.
"It helped me to birdie a lot of the par-fives and that was one of the reasons for my win. He's not getting it back now. I'm keeping it!"
Vaughan's charity, though, did not help the American who ended in joint 41st place with a two-over-par aggregate of 290.

Singh said after the third round on Saturday that he had always seen himself as a mediocre putter but, after returning to a conventional short putter after a winless 18 month period experimenting with the long 'broomhandle' style, he switched again at the suggestion of his wife.
"I was getting very frustrated at not winning. I wasn't putting badly but I just wasn't making enough 10-footers and birdies," he said.
"My wife told me to change back. Now I feel my best form is returning and my putting stroke is as good as it has ever been."
Price matched Singh shot for shot over the front nine with three birdies apiece. Both men birdied the par-five 11th and then Price narrowed the gap with another birdie at the 12th.

But two crucial moments turned the tournament. Price spun his tee shot back into water at the par-three 15th and made four while Singh splashed out of an awkward greenside bunker to save par with a 12-foot putt.

Then at the par-five 17th Singh missed the green with his third shot and finally sank a wretched 15-footer to save par while Price missed a simpler eight-footer for birdie. A potential two-shot swing was narrowly avoided.

Price then holed another pressure putt at the last to post a round of 68 and narrow the lead once again but Singh had only to two-putt from 20 feet to secure the win and a cheque for 529,300 rand ($119,000).
The expected challenge from defending champion Ernie Els of South Africa never materialised as putt after putt failed to drop for the world number four during a frustrating round of 70.
Zimbabwe's Mark McNulty and U.S.-based South African Fulton Allem posted rounds of 69 and 67 to catch Els on 275, 13 under par but a distant five shots from Singh and four from Price.
